text:
🇲🇽🛢️ <u>Trión deepwater oil field 71% complete</u>

Trión, Mexico's first ultra-deepwater oil project, off the coast of Tamaulipas, is now 71% complete, El Economista reports. The Woodside–Pemex development carries a $10.434 billion investment, 24 subsea wells and a gas tie-in to the South Texas–Tuxpan pipeline. First oil is due in 2028. Governor Américo Villarreal toured the Deepwater Thalassa drillship, and the state wants local suppliers and the ports of Matamoros, Altamira and Tampico to share in the work.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>PAN promises to cut the VAT that PAN raised</u>

PAN leader Jorge Romero is promising to cut VAT from 16% to 10%. He leaves out who set it at 16%: Felipe Calderón's government, whose 2010 tax package raised it from 15%, passed with PAN and PRI votes in the middle of a recession. El Soberano calls it selective memory.
banner: PAN: CUT THE VAT CALDERÓN RAISED

text:
🇲🇽🌎 <u>Nadia Beller is now safe in Mexico</u>

Nadia Beller, who sought asylum at Mexico's embassy in La Paz, has arrived in Mexico, President Sheinbaum confirmed. Beller reported threats and an attempted femicide by her ex-partner Fernando Cerimedo, the Argentine digital operative she also accuses of working elections across Latin America to destabilize progressive governments. Mexican authorities arranged her exit from the embassy. She will now meet with the SRE to decide whether to stay in Mexico or travel on.
banner: NADIA BELLER NOW SAFE IN MEXICO

text:
🔥🇲🇽 <u>94% of corruption complaints never reach a judge</u>

Of 1,300 criminal complaints filed by the Anti-Corruption and Good Government Ministry, only 80 have been taken to court, Miguel Badillo reports in Contralínea. That leaves 93.9% sitting with the FGR's anti-corruption prosecutor, María de la Luz Mijangos, who has held the post since 2019. Some cases expire before anyone files them. Ten months into Ernestina Godoy's shake-up of the FGR, not one of the ministry's sanctions against officials has triggered a single FGR investigation.

🇲🇽🇨🇦 <u>Sheinbaum and Carney: 120 joint initiatives done, trade up 18%</u>

On the APEC sidelines in Shenzhen, Sheinbaum and Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney reviewed the bilateral action plan they launched in September 2025. Carney said 120 of its initiatives are already done, and that trade between the two countries grew 18% in 2026 and 60% over five years. "We have an extraordinary relationship with Canada and agreed to expand it into the future," Sheinbaum said. Two USMCA partners compare notes in China while Washington stalls the treaty review.

🇲🇽🇨🇳 <u>Sheinbaum invites Xi Jinping to Mexico for APEC 2028</u>

In Shenzhen, President Sheinbaum met Xi Jinping and invited him to Mexico for the 2028 APEC summit, which Mexico will host. "We spoke of a new era of cooperation for development," she said. On the table: a more balanced trade relationship under Plan México, plus joint research in agriculture, biotechnology and clean energy. This comes days after Washington's ambassador lectured Mexico about Chinese imports.

🇲🇽🛍️ <u>Buen Fin at halftime: sales up 20%, 82% bought Mexican-made</u>

Halfway through Buen Fin 2026, Concanaco Servytur's preliminary survey puts sales 20% above a normal weekend on average, with 78% of businesses reporting an increase, El Economista reports. The 16th edition targets 235 billion pesos in sales, up 7.3% from 219.2 billion in 2025. Cards covered 82% of payments, 61% shopped in physical stores, and 82% said they bought products made in Mexico.

🇲🇽🤝 <u>Gobernación presses Triqui leaders to sign peace in Tierra Blanca Copala</u>

Interior Secretary Rosa Icela Rodríguez called on the leaders of the rival organizations in Tierra Blanca Copala, Oaxaca, to "finally sign peace" so some 500 displaced Triqui people can return home. They were driven out by an armed attack on December 26, 2020, almost six years ago. Federal and state officials entered the community on Friday the 13th to restart dialogue. Rodríguez was careful not to declare victory early: no celebrating until peace is guaranteed.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>One-year ban for the SRE official who held his wedding at MUNAL</u>

Mexico's Anti-Corruption and Good Government Ministry barred Martín Borrego Llorente, Alicia Bárcena's former chief of staff at the SRE, from public office for one year. He requested the National Art Museum's reception hall for what he billed as an official event. It was his wedding. Borrego, who resigned from Semarnat when the case broke, insists it was a diplomatic event paid for privately. His sanction is one of a package covering 82 public servants, one private individual and one company.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>UIF freezes accounts of Córdova-era INE director</u>

Mexico's Financial Intelligence Unit (UIF) added Juan Carlos Cuervo Escalona, the INE's director of coordination and analysis under Lorenzo Córdova, to its List of Blocked Persons over suspected illicit operations tied to electoral contracts. La Jornada links him to the Hernández Casillas brothers, the contractors at the center of the INE procurement scandal. Cuervo left the INE in 2023 and that same year became legal representative of Corporativo ZEG. The red flags: simulated bidding and alleged misuse of public money.
